item.title: The Big Asheville Science Salon! — Wed Sep 2, 5:00 PM
item.description: Welcome to the tremendous, amazing, Big Asheville Science Salon! SEPTEMBER: Diagnosing the Lesula monkey with evolutionary biologist Dr. James Fuller. “What’s in a name? That which we call a rose, By any other name would smell as sweet.” – W. ‘Wild Willy’ Shakespeare In a remote forest not far from Congo’s mighty Lomami River, researchers stumbled upon an odd looking monkey. Given that monkeys are not uncommon in rain forests and many, alas, are not classically handsome, such an occurrence is hardly remarkable. To the experienced field biologists, however, this particular primate proved peculiar because it looked completely unfamiliar. Sharing photos of the mysterious monkey with experts around the world was little help, with most responses ranging from “What the hell is that?” to “I guess it looks kinda like …” So, was this a “new” species? item.title: Flat Laurel Creek Rock Scramble — Sat Sep 5, 9:15 AM
item.description: The Asheville Hiking Group This is one of the most popular creek scrambles near Asheville. Note this is not the Flat Laurel Creek Trail, it is a creek hike. It begins at NC Hwy. 215 near the confluence of Flat Laurel Creek and the West Fork of the Pigeon River (35.3285, -82.9096), approximately, at about 9:30. We will ascend past numerous rapids and impressive waterfalls. We will be in the creek or rock hopping most of the day. The requirements are a good sense of balance, comfortable shoes with good traction, and ability or interest to hike and climb in a creek. Good swimming holes abound. The pace will be moderate, with time for pictures, and we will take a short break at one of the many scenic spots for lunch. After finishing the ascent we will trail hike up to the Black Balsam/Big Sam parking lot, where cars will be left for this shuttle. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.
Please arrive a few minutes early to say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.
Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!
A note about the format We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.
For our full event schedule, visit https://shutupwrite.com

item.title: Free Live Music: Jvnk Drawer — Thu Sep 24, 6:00 PM
item.description: Some bands write songs. Jvnk Drawer excavates them — pulling from a thirty-year vein of half-forgotten gems, salvaged riffs, and songs that were simply waiting for the right band to play them. The result is alternative rock with real mileage on it: melodies sharp enough to catch you off guard, lyrics honest enough to stick. At its center is Gavin Conner, a songwriter whose Asheville roots run back to 2007, when he arrived in town to join local favorites, If You Wannas. What followed was a long apprenticeship in the local scene — a solo run, countless stages, and a songbook that quietly grew into something few writers ever amass. By 2017, that songbook needed a band worthy of it, and Jvnk Drawer was born, with drummer Chris Peterson and bassist Erik Avots rounding out the lineup and giving the songs a pulse.
